transcript: Sometimes, the weirder a play gets, the more it makes sense to me, and this was entirely the case with Jordans at The Public. This bold and inventive new play by Ife Olujobi is about a receptionist named Jordan at a production studio who is terribly mistreated and has learned to navigate a space where she's consistently overlooked and undermined. When the company decides it wants to attract a more diverse clientele, conversations around workplace diversity come up, a new Jordan drops in, and let's just say things get real crazy real fast. It’s surreal and eerie and provocative kind of like a Black Mirror episode. At first, I felt like this play was just spewing ideas at the expense of developed characters, but the more ridiculous it got, the more I felt like I understood them and the tone of this piece is extremely distinct and commanding. Visual spoiler ahead so if you wanna experience this like I did scroll away now. This play is complex and layered and I'm sure I did not get all of it but I was thoroughly entertained and had plenty to think about. I think this play will be very decisive and as a credit to the production’s specificity in tone, topic, writing, and direction, I think that is a great thing. With that, another program for my collection.
